title: The Lighter Brief
overview: Big week in US politics: Mississippi's Senate race is still being counted, and President Trump picked Stephen Miller as his new chief of staff after the midterms. Elsewhere, Tesla is winding down Cybertruck production in Texas, Charlotte's I-77 toll lane project is back with a community-first pitch, and Doja Cat chatted about love and jealousy with Jennifer Hudson.

stories.headline: Mississippi's Senate race is still too close to call
stories.summary: Democrat Scott Colom leads Republican Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith by about 2,500 votes, but thousands of ballots are still being counted and no winner has been declared. Officials can't say exactly how many ballots remain, because Mississippi's 82 counties run their own elections and there are many provisional and late-arriving mail ballots. Both campaigns have legal teams ready.
key_facts: Colom leads by about 2,500 votes as of Friday night
Estimates of outstanding ballots range from about 15,000 provisional ballots (Colom campaign) to roughly 20,000 total (state GOP chair)
Voters have until Nov. 10 to resolve provisional ballots; certification deadline is Nov. 13
Mississippi has no provision for a vote recount
stories.why: It's a closely watched Senate seat, and the slow count is drawing attention to how Mississippi runs its elections and maintains its voter rolls.

stories.headline: Stephen Miller named White House chief of staff
stories.summary: President Trump announced Friday that longtime adviser Stephen Miller will replace Susie Wiles as chief of staff, starting Monday. The move follows Republicans losing control of Congress in Tuesday's midterms. Miller is best known for shaping the administration's immigration enforcement policies. Wiles, the first woman to hold the job, will keep working for Trump on political operations.
key_facts: Miller takes over on Monday; he was previously deputy chief of staff
Wiles submitted her resignation Thursday night; sources told Axios it was a mutual decision
Democratic leaders Hakeem Jeffries and Chuck Schumer criticized the pick
Separately, a federal judge paused construction of Trump's planned arch near the Lincoln Memorial for 14 days
stories.why: The chief of staff controls access to the president and negotiates with Congress, so this choice signals how the White House may approach a Democratic-led Congress.

stories.headline: Tesla to wind down Cybertruck production in Texas
stories.summary: Elon Musk said Tesla will wind down Cybertruck production at its Texas factory around mid-2027 to make room for more Cybercab robotaxis. The truck has had disappointing sales, recalls and quality issues since its 2023 launch. Musk didn't say whether production will move elsewhere or stop entirely.
key_facts: Wind-down planned around the middle of 2027
The Cybertruck is only built at Tesla's Austin, Texas factory
The space will go to Cybercab production
disputed: Confirmed: production is winding down in Texas. Unclear: whether the Cybertruck will be built somewhere else or discontinued.
stories.why: It's a sign of Tesla shifting its focus toward self-driving robotaxis.

stories.headline: Silfab Solar plans restart at Fort Mill plant
stories.summary: Silfab Solar will restart its chemical commissioning process at its Fort Mill, S.C., plant on Monday. Work had been paused since March after two chemical leaks. The company says it completed a thorough review of the facility and its procedures.
key_facts: 72-hour notice given Friday to the SC Department of Environmental Services
Work paused since March after two chemical leaks
Restarting commissioning doesn't mean manufacturing begins immediately
stories.why: Nearby residents have followed this plant closely, so it's good to know what's resuming and when.

stories.headline: I-77 toll lane project is back, with neighbors invited to weigh in
stories.summary: NCDOT leaders spoke publicly Friday about the revived I-77 South toll lane project, stressing that the community will help shape it. A community engagement center has reopened where people can share design ideas and suggest discounts like toll rate caps. Construction isn't expected until the 2030s.
key_facts: At least $300 million in community benefits tied to the project
Charlotte City Council votes Monday on a working group to oversee those benefits
Design is only 10% to 15% complete; four developers are competing
stories.why: Residents have a real chance to influence a big local project early, possibly including funding for a grocery store off West Boulevard.

stories.headline: EU tells TikTok to change its For You feed
stories.summary: The European Union says TikTok's recommendation algorithm can pull users, especially kids, into 'rabbit holes' of harmful content, breaking its Digital Services Act. It wants bigger design changes, such as giving more weight to users' stated preferences, or TikTok could face large fines. TikTok says the EU's claims are inaccurate.
key_facts: EU says the 'not interested' button may not be enough to change the feed
Suggested fixes include not using viewing time to recommend content
Follows a February EU demand to change 'addictive design' features
disputed: These are EU findings; TikTok rejects them and can respond before any penalty.
stories.why: It could change how one of the world's most popular apps decides what people see.

links.title: EU tells TikTok to change ‘harmful’ For You feed

stories.headline: Free flu shots available across Jamaica
stories.summary: Jamaican health officials are encouraging people to get the flu vaccine, now free at public health centres and hospitals for priority groups. Flu season usually runs October to March. Others can get the shot privately for a fee.
key_facts: Priority groups include pregnant women, healthcare workers, and people 65+ with chronic conditions
Flu vaccination is recommended every year
High-risk people with flu symptoms should seek care promptly
disputed: The flu vaccine is an established, routinely recommended vaccine.
stories.why: A simple, free step that helps protect vulnerable people this season.

links.title: Jamaicans encouraged to get Flu vaccine

stories.headline: Jamaica's Government and Opposition to meet after heated session
stories.summary: After a tense House session on Tuesday, Opposition leader of government business Phillip Paulwell agreed to meet Government representatives Monday at Speaker Juliet Holness's invitation. He welcomed the talks but criticized the Speaker's handling of a debate on the Opposition's censure motion.
key_facts: Meeting set for Monday
Paulwell hopes for 'a frank and constructive dialogue among equals'
He suggested a mediator could be involved if needed
stories.why: Both sides agreeing to sit down is a step toward calmer parliamentary business.

links.title: Gov’t, Opposition agree to meet Monday after Parliament ruckus
